text:
mira: Heads up — seeing 'Event loop is closed' + fd/socket warnings when running the async python SDK under uvicorn with reload. Happens after a few reloads, looks like an httpx connector/socket leak.

mira: minimal repro: start uvicorn --reload and hit endpoint a few times, then Ctrl+C + restart -> crash. stack: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed

mira: repro code:```py
from redwood import AsyncInferenceClient
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncInferenceClient(api_key="$RD_KEY")

@app.get("/infer")
async def infer():
    # naive: sdk creates its own httpx AsyncClient internally per request
    r = await client.generate("hello")
    return {"out": r.text}
```

dan: hmm, do you call client.close() on shutdown? uvicorn --reload forks and reloads, you can leak sockets if AsyncClient isn't closed.

mira: i don't. i assumed gc/atexit would close it.

javi: GC isn't reliable. You should either use an app lifespan or async context manager. Example:```py
@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup():
    await client.__aenter__()  # or await client.startup() if provided

@app.on_event("shutdown")
async def shutdown():
    await client.__aexit__(None, None, None)
```
But that relies on SDK exposing proper async CM methods.

tim: another angle — httpx AsyncClient has a default connector pool that can leak when processes are reloaded. If the SDK constructs a new AsyncClient per call (anti-pattern) you get sockets piling up. SDK should reuse a single AsyncClient instance per AsyncInferenceClient.

mira: confirmed — our code path creates a new httpx.AsyncClient for every request. oof.

javi: feature ask: SDK should either: (a) expose a `get_async_session()` that returns the shared AsyncClient, or (b) internally keep a singleton AsyncClient and provide explicit `close()`/context manager. Also add types: typing for AsyncInferenceClient should indicate __aenter__/__aexit__ return types for mypy.

dan: +1 on typings. Also noticed auth refresh races: if two reqs see 401 at same time, both attempt refresh concurrently, causing intermittent failures. Async needs an asyncio.Lock around token refresh.

mira: ran into that too. one request gets new token, other overwrote token with older value in our retry handler.

javi: workaround: add a global asyncio.Lock in your app around client.refresh_token calls. But SDK should handle it. Filing an issue.

sdk-bot: Thanks for the report — created GH issue: redwood/redwood-python#1428 - "async client: connection pooling, lifecycle, and auth refresh race". Please attach repro and logs.

mira: attaching logs + small repro gist here: https://gist.github.com/mira/abcd1234

tim: quick workaround for uvicorn reload: set --reload-delay and call `await client.close()` in a shutdown handler. For Windows CI weirdness, you might also need `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())` before starting uvicorn.

dan: devex TODOs: 1) SDK: make AsyncInferenceClient reuse httpx.AsyncClient 2) add explicit async close() and async context manager 3) guard token refresh with lock 4) add docs snippet for FastAPI/uvicorn lifespan

mira: thanks — that should unblock my service. i'll try the startup/shutdown patch and comment on the GH issue with results. :thumbsup:
